title: Reverse Periodization for Improving Sports Performance: A Systematic Review
claims: A total of 11 studies were identified in this systematic review of reverse periodization.
Two studies compared block periodization and reverse periodization, while nine compared traditional periodization and reverse periodization.
Reverse periodization appears to be no more effective than other forms of periodization in improving sports performance, muscular endurance, maximum strength, or maximal oxygen uptake.
Reverse periodization likely induces similar improvements to a traditional model in shorter events such as the 100-m swimming event.
The authors state that more comparative studies are required to verify the effectiveness and utility of reverse periodization across endurance sports.
